title_ar: فتاوي في قضايا معاصرة في الأنكحة 3
title_en: Fatwas on contemporary questions concerning marriage 3
body_ar: حكم استعمال الحبوب والحقن لمنع الحمل ماحكم استعمال الحبوب والحقن لمنع الحمل و هل يجوز للمرأة أن تستعملها إذا كانت تخاف الولادة والحال أن لها جنينا؟ إن على المسلمات أن يعلمن أن هذه الأمة تتعرض لمؤامرة دولية عظيمة يقصد بها تقليل أفرادها فليس لدى أمة الإسلام قوة ضاربة إلا عدد أفرادها والأمم الكافرة تسعى لتقليل أعداد المسلمين وقد قرأت في تقرير في الولايات المتحدة الأمريكية أن الأفارقة امتنعوا عن تنفيذ مخططات تحديد النسل فليس لهم حل ولا علاج إلا بإثارة الحروب الطاحنة فيما بينهم إن أعداء الله يخططون لتقليل سواد المسلمين ولنقص أعدادهم فعلى المسلمين ألا ينخدعوا بهذه الدعاية
body_en:
The ruling on using pills and injections to prevent pregnancy. What is the ruling on using pills and injections to prevent pregnancy, and is it permissible for a woman to use them if she fears childbirth, while she is carrying a child?

Muslim women must know that this ummah is exposed to a great international conspiracy whose purpose is to reduce the number of its members. The Muslim ummah has no striking force except the number of its members, and the disbelieving nations strive to reduce the numbers of the Muslims. I have read in a report in the United States of America that the Africans refused to carry out the birth-control schemes, so that there is no solution and no remedy for them except by stirring up grinding wars among them. The enemies of God plan to reduce the great mass of the Muslims and to diminish their numbers. So the Muslims must not be taken in by this propaganda.

flags.arabic: ماحكم استعمال الحبوب والحقن لمنع الحمل و هل يجوز للمرأة أن تستعملها إذا كانت تخاف الولادة والحال أن لها جنينا؟
flags.context: the question asks for a ruling on contraception; the published text gives no ruling at all before breaking off
options: withhold from publication until the full text behind the .docx download is obtained
publish with a prominent banner stating that no ruling is given in the published text
publish the excerpt as it stands
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY, and the clearest case of it in this slice. The questioner asks two precise fiqh questions — whether contraceptive pills and injections may be used, and whether a woman who fears childbirth may use them while pregnant. The published text answers neither. It moves at once to a general exhortation about Muslim numbers and then stops. A reader will take that exhortation as the ruling, i.e. as a prohibition of contraception, which the Sheikh does not state here. The second limb of the question is a medical one touching a pregnant woman's health, which makes publishing a non-answer as though it were an answer particularly hazardous. The full material is behind the .docx download in source_download_link.

flags.arabic: وقد قرأت في تقرير في الولايات المتحدة الأمريكية أن الأفارقة امتنعوا عن تنفيذ مخططات تحديد النسل فليس لهم حل ولا علاج إلا بإثارة الحروب الطاحنة فيما بينهم
flags.context: the Sheikh's report of what he has read concerning birth-control schemes in Africa
options: translate faithfully, with no editorial gloss in the body
translate faithfully and attach an editorial note on the page
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW REQUIRED — this flag is about publication, not the translation, which is faithful and has been neither softened nor strengthened. The passage asserts an international conspiracy to reduce Muslim numbers and reports, as something read in an American document, that wars are deliberately fomented in Africa where birth-control schemes fail. No source is named. Published in English without context this carries reputational risk, and in some jurisdictions the framing of 'the disbelieving nations' and 'the enemies of God' may engage local rules on incitement. The decision whether and how to publish belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office, never to the translator. Option 2 would alter the record and is offered only for completeness.

flags.context: the source runs the question and the answer together in a single paragraph with no break
options: insert a paragraph break between question and answer in body_en only, keeping body_ar as served
keep both as a single paragraph
insert the break in both body_ar and body_en
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT. Unlike every other record in this range, this one has no paragraph break between the question and the answer; the answer begins at 'inna ʿalā al-muslimāt an yaʿlamna' with no separator. body_ar preserves the source exactly. body_en inserts the break so that the English does not read as though the questioner himself were making the assertions about the conspiracy — which would be a substantive misattribution. The break is therefore editorial and is recorded here rather than made silently.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

In the source, the answer begins with the elliptical particle 'anna ('[the answer is] that ...'), the Joomla fatwa template's standing form. The English drops the particle and begins the sentence directly; no content is added or removed by this.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off with no ruling and a .docx download is offered ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends; nothing has been supplied to complete the answer. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.
'Ummah' is left untranslated as established in English usage. 'The great mass of the Muslims' renders sawād al-muslimīn, their main body or bulk.

The answer as published contains no ruling word at all — no ḥukm, no jāʾiz, no ḥarām is applied to the pills or the injections. The English therefore contains none either. This absence is the point of the critical_for_display flag.
